dedupe_keys.name: building damage assessment after the 19 september 2017 puebla earthquake mexico city calle la morena street case

description: This case study reports a field damage assessment of buildings in Mexico City after the earthquake of 19 September 2017, which caused heavy damage in the capital and in the state of Morelos. It is published in Frontiers in Built Environment (4 December 2018) by Samuel Roeslin, Quincy T. M. Ma and Hugón Juárez García, from a reconnaissance team from New Zealand. The authors argue that post-earthquake damage data from around the world are hard to combine because surveys lack consistent methods and definitions, and propose a paper-based assessment form built on the Global Earthquake Model building taxonomy (version 2.0) and the European Macroseismic Scale EMS-98. They tested it along one street, Calle La Morena, and present a new visualisation of damage against building characteristics that highlights the drivers of damage. Coverage: damage across Mexico City, with the detailed street study in Calle La Morena. Access: open-access article with PDF. Licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0; free. Caveats: one street sample and a paper form; the collected data are shown in the article, not released as a dataset. Simulation uses: consistent damage observations for calibrating fragility and exposure models. Related records: the Türkiye earthquake damage datasets and the Irpinia empirical fragility data.
name: Building damage assessment after the 19 September 2017 Puebla earthquake, Mexico City (Calle La Morena street case)
outcomes: A New Zealand team assessed damage across Mexico City and tested a new paper survey form, based on the GEM taxonomy and EMS-98, along Calle La Morena, where a street-level visualisation showed how damage correlated with building features.
